transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

A warm fridge with a cold freezer is almost always an airflow problem in a frost-free model. The single cooling coil sits in the freezer, and a fan pushes that cold air into the fridge section. If that airflow is blocked (usually by ice) or the fan has stopped, the freezer stays cold but the fridge warms up. The most common cause is a defrost system failure where ice builds up on the coils and chokes off the air. Less commonly, it could be the fan motor itself. 1. Is the freezer actually still cold (you can test with a thermometer or by checking if ice cream is hard)?
2. Look inside the freezer at the back wall: is there a thick block of ice or heavy frost covering the coils?
Freezer's fine, about -16C on the thermometer. There's some frost on the back wall but not loads. Fridge is reading 10C.

Thanks for checking that. A reading of -16C in the freezer suggests the compressor and cooling system are working correctly, which isolates the problem to airflow between the two sections. The most likely cause remains a defrost fault where ice has built up behind the back panel (even if you can't see it yet) and is blocking the cold air from reaching the fridge. 1. With the freezer door shut, listen closely to the back wall area. Can you hear a faint humming or whirring sound (the evaporator fan running), or is it completely silent?
2. If you can hear the fan, does the air coming out of the vent into the fridge section feel cold and move strongly, or is there little/no airflow?
I can hear it running a lot, yes. I can't see any vent in the fridge though, so I'm not sure about the airflow. No burning smell or tripping, by the way.

Because you are renting and cannot take the appliance out to dismantle the rear panel, we need a diagnostic test that doesn't require tools. The standard way to confirm if this is an ice blockage (caused by a failed defrost heater or thermostat) is to perform a full manual defrost. Please switch the fridge-freezer off at the wall socket, remove all food (keeping perishables in cool bags with ice if possible), and leave both doors open for 24 hours. Make sure any melted water is mopped up so it doesn't damage your kitchen floor. Once everything is dry, plug it back in. Does the fridge return to a normal cold temperature (around 4C) after this?
I can do that, but it means emptying everything and I haven't tried it yet. Is there anything simpler I should check first? Otherwise I may need to report it through the letting agent.

There isn't a simpler check that will fix this. The symptoms (cold freezer, warm fridge, fan running) point strongly to an internal ice blockage behind the freezer's back panel, caused by a failed defrost component (heater or thermostat). Because you are renting and cannot dismantle the appliance to clear the ice or replace the part, this is not something you can fix yourself safely. Please report this to your letting agent as a repair request. Explain that the fridge section has warmed up while the freezer remains cold, which indicates a defrost system fault requiring engineer access to the internal components.

claimsRejected.claim: Also, since you mentioned a power cut recently, please ensure both doors are closed and left shut for 24 hours to see if it recovers on its own, as sometimes systems just need time to reset after a power loss.
